sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule. Learned APP waives service of Rule on behalf of the Respondent State.

2. The applicant has filed this Application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.11203024230666 of 2023 registered with Junagadh City 'B' Division Police Station, District:Junagadh for the offences punishable under Sections 306 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Junagadh City 'B' Division Police Station, District:Junagadh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned advocate Mr.Ashish Dagli for the applicant.

He submitted that in the present case,
investigation of the offence is over and charge-sheet is filed.
The applicant happens to be husband of the deceased.

The applicant had a strong reason to believe that his wife was having an affair with some stranger and therefore, a quarrel had taken place between them NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4881/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined prior to the incident, because of which, the deceased had committed suicide.

The applicant has the screenshot of chats, which had Hardik Kishorbhai Jebaliya vs State Of Gujarat on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45400267/
1 taken place between the deceased and the unknown person, which indicate that the relation between the deceased and the said unknown person was not merely of a friendship and therefore, it was very much genuine for the present applicant to have inquired about the same from the deceased, for which the deceased felt offended and committed suicide along with their son, aged two years.

sentences.text:
He,
therefore, submitted to allow the present application and enlarge the present applicant on bail subject to suitable conditions.

4. The application is opposed by learned APP Mr.Pandya inter alia contending that the present applicant is trying to project his own wife to be of 'easy virtues' for procuring a favourable order in the present application.
The relation between the deceased and the unknown person was merely of a friendship and there was no reason for the applicant to doubt upon the character of the deceased.
4.1 He further submitted that the present applicant used to torture the deceased for her having such friendly relation with another person, whom she believed to be her brother.
The married life of the deceased and the applicant was merely three years.

The incident has attained seriousness because the deceased had committed suicide with her son, who was aged two years at the time of incident,
which is indicative of the fact that the present applicant had subjected the deceased to physical and mental torture to such an extent that she had no other option but to commit suicide.
He therefore submitted to dismiss NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4881/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined the present application.
5. This Court has considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for the parties and has also perused the material placed on record.
As per the case of prosecution, on 27.8.2023 the deceased along with her son had committed suicide by jumping on railway track in front of a running train.
6. Upon perusal of the investigation papers, it appears that the marriage life of the present applicant and the deceased was merely of three years.

The record further indicates that the deceased was found by the present applicant to be chatting on the social media platform with some unknown person, namely Mohit, however, on that occasion, the applicant did not take any cognizance of the same, nor took any action, because he wanted to save his marriage and also wanted to see that the life of newly born child may not be affected.
7. After some time, the deceased was found to be chatting with another unknown person, namely Ajay, on the social media platform.
The deceased had saved the mobile number of the said Ajay in her mobile phone as 'Nehall'.
The applicant has also produced the screenshot of the chats, which had taken place between the deceased and the said Ajay.
Upon perusal of the same, it appears that the applicant had a valid reason for warning his wife, i.e. deceased, not to indulge in such activity.
He had also threatened the deceased that he would come out of the marriage.

8. Having regard to the nature of chats which had taken NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4881/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined place between the applicant and said Ajay, it prima facie appears that the relationship between them were not merely of a friendship,
nor the same were of brother and sister.

If the relation between the deceased and the said Ajay were Hardik Kishorbhai Jebaliya vs State Of Gujarat on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45400267/
2 of brother and sister, as is sought to be claimed by the prosecution, there was no reason for the deceased to hide the said fact from her own husband, i.e. present applicant.

Considering the same,
the application deserves consideration.
9. This court has considered the following aspects:

(a) As per catena of decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court, there are mainly 3 factors which are required to be considered by this court i.e. prima facie case, availability of Applicant accused at the time of trial and tampering and hampering with the witnesses by the accused.
(b) That the learned Advocate for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant Accused is not likely to flee away.
(c) That the Applicant is in custody since 7.11.2023.

(d) The law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v.
C.B.I. Reported in (2012) 1 SCC 40.
10.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned Advocates for the parties and perusing the record produced in this case as well as taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations, gravity of accusation, availability of the Applicant Accused at the time of Trial etc. and the role attributed to the present Applicant accused, the present Application deserves to be allowed and accordingly stands allowed.

This Court has also gone through the FIR and police papers and also the earlier order passed by the learned Sessions Court where the learned Sessions Judge NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4881/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined has disallowed the bail Application at initial stage.

The Applicant Accused is ordered to be released on bail in connection with the aforesaid FIR on executing a personal bond of Rs.10,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, subject to the following conditions that he shall:
(a) not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the fact of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any Police Officer or tamper with the evidence.
(b) maintain law and order and not to indulge in any criminal activities.

(c) furnish the documentary proof of complete, correct and present address of residence to the Investigating Officer and to the Trial Court at the time of executing the bond and shall not change the residence without prior permission of the trial Court.
(d) provide contact numbers as well as the contact numbers of the sureties before the Trial Court.
In case of change in such numbers inform in writing immediately to the trial Court.
